clues.text: A neighbourhood in the western part of Kamloops, in British Columbia, Canada. It sits just north of the Thompson River.
clues.narrowing: rules out everything outside western British Columbia

source.quote: Brocklehurst is a neighbourhood in the western area of Kamloops, British Columbia, Canada. Brocklehurst is bordered by the Thompson River to the south, North Shore to the east, Tranquille to the west, and the Batchelor hills and Batchelor Heights aka Batchelor Hills to the north.

clues.text: This is the warmest small climate spot in its city. It can be four degrees warmer than another part of the same city.
clues.narrowing: rules out the cooler parts of the same city

source.quote: The Brocklehurst area (or Brock, as referred to by its residents), is the warmest and most hospitable of the micro-climates in the city of Kamloops. There can be as much as a 4 degree Celsius increase from Brock to Aberdeen, all within the city of Kamloops.

clues.text: For a short time, it was a district town of its own. Then it joined Kamloops in 1973.
clues.narrowing: rules out neighbourhoods that did not join the city in 1973

source.quote: Brocklehurst, which briefly existed as a district municipality in its own right from 1971 until amalgamation with Kamloops in 1973, is the largest of the city's neighbourhoods, accounting for 16% of the city's population.

clues.text: It takes its name from a man from Liverpool, England. He lived here from 1896 to 1907.
clues.narrowing: rules out places not named for a Liverpool man who lived there

source.quote: The community is named after Ernest Brocklehurst, from Liverpool, England who lived in the area between 1896 and 1907.

clues.text: Look north from its streets to see the Batchelor Hills. They mark the top edge of this part of the city.
